page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.4xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz. The instance is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage options. Network performance is anchored by a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance primarily in the average tier for multi-core operations and memory bandwidth. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance score of 11469.52 and Geekbench multi-core score of 6841.0 reflect steady parallel processing capabilities. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1150.39. Memory bandwidth tests show average read performance at 54.29 GB/sec for large blocks, though large-block write performance is weaker at 24.73 GB/sec.

Given its balanced resource allocation and dedicated CPU cores, this instance is suitable for general-purpose workloads such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 10.85 GB/sec, and database operations, scoring 5002.27 in Passmark database tests. It also handles Redis SET operations efficiently at 12.97 million operations per second. While it can process small language model inference workloads, performance drops significantly on medium models, making it less suitable for complex AI tasks. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated physical cores offer predictable performance for standard enterprise applications without the premium associated with high-performance compute or memory-optimized hardware classes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.cm4.4xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2667 v4 processor running at 3.2 GHz. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and operates on the KVM hypervisor with a 6 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 6841.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 14861.27, though single-core performance and large-block memory write speeds are relatively weak. This hardware profile is well-suited for standard enterprise workloads, including static web serving, Redis databases, and moderate multi-threaded application processing, offering a predictable, dedicated resource pool for general-purpose computing tasks.
